answer: Verified at merge commit 70b83631 (not working tree, which is a sibling branch behind PR12). The structural move is LEGITIMATE and CORRECT: infra/kyverno/ is the canonical admission-policy root, established by ADR-0039 (lines 104-108, names infra/kyverno/policies/require-signed-images.yaml as the kyverno enforcement file) and ADR-0041 (lines 117-118, merge-queue serializes any PR touching infra/kyverno/policies/**; line 135 CODEOWNERS infra/ → @foundry @cloud). ADR-0052 inventory line 189 already classified oyatie/infra/ as the policy-as-code root with KEEP status. The parallel deploy/gitops/ root was a single-file leaf with no doctrine backing — collapsing it under infra/ is P9_no_sprawl-aligned. Move is path-only; no kind/scope/concept BNF impact (P14 BNF governs durable-artifact filenames under specs/registries/evidence/templates/adrs/standards/plans — infra/ is none of those, it is repo-top-level IaC/policy and lives outside the BNF scope, consistent with how contracts/ and crates/ and scripts/ also sit outside P14). At merge: deploy/ is fully removed from the tree (git ls-tree 70b83631 confirms no deploy node), and the 7 inbound refs across 5 files (kernel lib.rs ×3, app main.rs ×1, three evidence JSONs ×3) all rewrite to the new path consistently. Argo self-referential `path:` inside application.json also rewritten. STRUCTURAL DRIFT FROM ADR-0117 ITSELF: ADR-0117 §'Naming justification' asserts 'infra/kyverno/ is the established admission-policy root' as if self-evident, but FAILS TO CITE ADR-0039 + ADR-0041 + ADR-0052 which actually establish it. Per the prevention-doctrine (every assertion should cite the canonical rule, not assert it), this is a soft ADR-quality issue rather than a structural-correctness issue. ADDITIONAL DRIFT: docs/DESIGN.md §8 'The flat target shape' (line 456) still lists `deploy/` as a canonical top-level directory ('per-deployable Helm/IaC, split out of services/'), now stale — the directory no longer exists and ADR-0117 did not update DESIGN.md to reflect the consolidation under infra/. This is a documentation-source-of-truth drift introduced by the PR not cleaning up the contradiction it created.

findings.summary: ADR-0117 §'Naming justification' asserts 'infra/kyverno/ is the established admission-policy root' without citing ADR-0039 (lines 104-108) + ADR-0041 (lines 117-118, 135) + ADR-0052 (line 189) which actually establish it. Violates the cite-the-canonical-rule discipline; future agents reading ADR-0117 in isolation cannot trace the structural justification.
findings.recommended_action: Amend ADR-0117 §'Naming justification' to cite: 'Canonical per ADR-0039 §Admission policy via Kyverno (line 107 names infra/kyverno/policies/require-signed-images.yaml), ADR-0041 §Merge queue lines 117-118 (merge-queue serializes infra/kyverno/policies/**) and §CODEOWNERS line 135 (infra/ → @foundry @cloud), and ADR-0052 inventory line 189 (oyatie/infra/ KEEP A8 policy-as-code).' Land as a docs-only follow-up PR.

findings.summary: docs/DESIGN.md §8 'The flat target shape' line 456 still lists `deploy/` as a canonical top-level directory (`per-deployable Helm/IaC (split out of services/)`). findings.recommended_action: Either (a) remove the `deploy/` line from DESIGN.md §8 flat-target-shape block and add `infra/` (kyverno/argo-rollouts policy + IaC) in its place, or (b) if Helm charts are still expected to land under deploy/ in the future, restate that intent in ADR-0117 §Consequences and mark this PR as the kyverno-only consolidation. Either path requires touching DESIGN.md. Land as a docs-only follow-up PR.

findings.summary: P14_file_naming_layout BNF (kind ∈ specs|registries|evidence|templates|adrs|standards|plans) does not enumerate `infra/` (or `contracts/`, `crates/`, `scripts/`, `.github/`). The doctrine implicitly carves out infra/policy/IaC root-level directories. No active violation — this is a doctrine-spec gap not introduced by PR12 — but PR12 was an opportunity to surface the carve-out explicitly via a tiny P14 amendment naming `infra/` as a sanctioned non-durable root.
findings.recommended_action: Optional: in a separate doctrine PR, amend specs/cross-cutting/oyatie-doctrine.json P14 to add a `non_durable_top_level_dirs` enum (or equivalent) listing `infra/`, `contracts/`, `crates/`, `scripts/`, `.github/` so future agents do not flag infra/ as a BNF-violation. Out of scope for PR12.
